READ_ME: The structure of a 1040 and all its dependencies is stored in this JSON
_schema: Tax form structure: jurisdiction-year → form → cells (and optional blocks for zero-to-many sections). Form 1040 and its worksheets.
_comments: Cell keys match Form 1040 line numbers/letters. Worksheets are modeled as forms with names like f1040_Lines_5a_and_5b.
value: current cell value; for now set equal to default.
description: matches what is written on the form or worksheet. explanation: more detail when needed (can be same as description).
blocks: repeating sections (0 to many entries). Each block has item_cells (schema for one entry), entries (array of objects), and optional min_entries/max_entries.
Block cell naming: block_id.index.field_name — e.g. w2.0.box_1, dependents.1.ssn. Index is 0-based. In equations: sum(w2.*.box_1) = sum of box_1 over all w2 entries; w2.0.box_1 = first W-2 box 1.

W-2 recipient: each entry has recipient = 'taxpayer' or 'spouse' for joint returns. Line 1 data flows from W-2 block: 1a = sum of W-2 box 1; multiple W-2s supported. W-2 is employer-furnished; sample/blank form: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2--2025.pdf

User-entered sources: Forms furnished by employers, brokerages, or payers (W-2, 1099s, 1098s) have no instructions in-app; the user enters data from the copies they received. These blocks/sources are listed in _user_entered_sources.

Multi-entry cells: Some form boxes take multiple entries (e.g. W-2 Box 12: code + amount per line). Use type "repeating" with item_cells and entries. Reference: block_id.index.field_name.sub_index.sub_field — e.g. w2.0.box_12.0.code, w2.0.box_12.1.amount.
